findings.title: Use === and !==, never == or !=
findings.message: Replace loose equality operators (==, !=) with strict equality (===, !==). The diff changed multiple strict equality checks to loose equality, which can hide type-coercion bugs.

claims.claim: The diff changed strict equality checks to loose equality operators.
claims.reason: The diff shows multiple lines where === was replaced with == and !== was replaced with !=. Specifically: line 13 changes `order.status === "pending"` to `order.status == "pending"`, line 16 changes `order.couponCode !== null` to `order.couponCode != null`, line 19 changes `order.user.role === "admin"` to `order.user.role == "admin"`, line 22 changes `order.tier !== "free"` to `order.tier != "free"`, and line 25 changes `order.shippingMethod === "express"` to `order.shippingMethod == "express"`. This directly demonstrates the change from strict to loose equality.

claims.claim: Loose equality operators (==, !=) should never be used.
claims.reason: The rule document explicitly states 'Use === and !==, never == or !='. This is the core principle of the rule.

claims.claim: Loose equality performs type coercion that can hide bugs.
claims.reason: The rule document states 'Loose equality performs type coercion that hides bugs' and provides examples like '"0" == false, null == undefined, etc.'

claims.claim: Strict equality (===, !==) should be used instead of loose equality.
claims.reason: The rule document explicitly recommends using strict equality operators (===, !==) and provides examples of good code using these operators.
